primary_responsibility: Manages user authentication workflows and session lifecycle, including credential verification, secure token generation, and session validation.

functional_group_candidates.name: User Authentication
functional_group_candidates.user_goal: Securely verify user identity and track login activity
business_rules: User must exist in the system to authenticate
Password must match the stored hash using SHA-256
Last login timestamp must be updated upon successful authentication

functional_group_candidates.name: Session Management
functional_group_candidates.user_goal: Maintain and validate secure user sessions for persistent access
business_rules: Session tokens must be cryptographically secure (URL-safe)
Validation requires the session to be non-expired relative to current UTC time

quality_issues.title: Insecure Password Hashing Algorithm
quality_issues.why_it_matters: SHA-256 is a fast cryptographic hash function, making it vulnerable to high-speed brute-force and hardware-accelerated (GPU/ASIC) cracking attacks. Furthermore, this implementation lacks a salt, making it susceptible to rainbow table attacks where identical passwords result in identical hashes.
quality_issues.suggested_fix: Replace hashlib.sha256 with a dedicated password hashing library like 'argon2-cffi' or 'bcrypt' which handles salting and adaptive work factors automatically.

quality_issues.title: Timing Attack Vulnerability in Password Verification
quality_issues.why_it_matters: The standard '==' operator performs a character-by-character comparison and returns as soon as a mismatch is found. This allows an attacker to infer the correct hash by measuring the time taken for the comparison.
quality_issues.suggested_fix: Use 'secrets.compare_digest()' or 'hmac.compare_digest()' for constant-time string comparison.

quality_issues.title: Transaction Mismanagement and Lack of Error Handling
quality_issues.why_it_matters: The service performs commits internally without handling rollbacks in case of failures. If an error occurs during or after a partial database operation, the session might be left in an inconsistent state. Additionally, hardcoded commits inside a service prevent the caller from managing larger atomic transactions.
quality_issues.suggested_fix: Wrap database operations in try/except blocks with 'self.db.rollback()' on failure, or move the commit responsibility to the caller/unit-of-work pattern.

quality_issues.title: Inconsistent Timezone Handling and Deprecated Methods
quality_issues.why_it_matters: Using 'datetime.utcnow()' creates naive datetime objects (without timezone info), which can lead to subtle bugs when comparing times across different system configurations. Furthermore, 'utcnow()' is deprecated in Python 3.12+.
quality_issues.suggested_fix: Use 'datetime.now(timezone.utc)' to ensure all datetime objects are timezone-aware and future-proof.

opportunities: Implement a 'logout' or 'revoke_session' method to allow users to manually invalidate tokens.
Implement 'sliding expiration' in 'validate_session' by updating the 'expires_at' timestamp upon successful use.
Add an 'is_active' or 'is_locked' check on the User model during authentication to prevent disabled accounts from logging in.
Dependency inject the hashing logic to improve testability and allow for easier algorithm migrations in the future.
